  • The Michigan State players didn't look that excited.

  • Oklahoma did.

  • I predict Alabama vs. Oklahoma on Jan 11

  • Pollack said that Alabama does have the best matchup b/c Bama wouldn't want to deal with Deshaun Watson. Connor Cook is [a fun guy to hit], and if Oklahoma does win, Mayfield would be a better matchup than Watson.

  • Rece says that there's a conspiracy out there that the committee moved Mich St above Oklahoma so that Alabama didn't have to face Oklahoma first, ostensibly then facing Clemson in the championship game.   • Jeff Long derps on about the logic of his fallible human committee (which not-so-secretly relies on computers to create their rankings).

  • Clemson describe as "clearly the #1 team in the nation."

  • There were people in the room that felt like Oklahoma could be the #1 team on the board.

  • Was there ever a question about the Big12 Championship game being a play-in game? Avoids the question, but we know it was.

Nick Saban comes on.

  • Predictably talks about expectations, how are you gonna respond, etc. Points out that having lost a game is unacceptable, but they responded well to it so I guess we'll settle for a playoff spot...haha, fucking Saban. He complains about us never being satisfied with his results, but he's never satisfied with his players' results, so I think it's fair. But damn, I love the guy, and he's been loosening up since 2011.

  • Tells a cool story about how Florida scored and they put Derrick Henry back in, and how happy Henry was to run the ball (he loves football btw), and how happy that made him...this presumably means most players would be happy to get a breather, but Henry wanted to keep playing.

  • We were too happy to get into the playoff last year. He says we don't really care about where we placed or why, it doesn't matter, we're in, let's get to work. Last year some players wondered why they were having to work once they got into the playoffs.

Dabo on now:

  • "We weren't always pretty, but championship teams find a way to win." Haha, sounds like he's describing Michigan State.

  • Dabo's laugh was a little uneasy when Oklahoma came up, even admits that "We're not that much better than Oklahoma." Says last year's game doesn't even matter right now (Clemson walloped Oklahoma 40-6).

  • Points out that some fundamentals are lost in the down-time, so that's the first thing they'll practice.

  • His #1 goal was to become a "consistent program." His message in 2011 was to stay focused and learn from success/failure. Bunch of other coach rhetoric. Kind of a boring guy when he's talking, you'd never tell from his body language. Maybe he's just tired. All those carbs.

Stoops still nowhere to be found, was absent with Baker Mayfield earlier.

  • WR Sterling Shepard interviews with Sam Ponder

I guess Dantonio is later, they go back to the studio.

  • Rece says Oklahoma is playing better than anyone, and they recognize Deshaun Watson's offense.

  • Pollack says Watson throws the best deep ball in America. Galloway says he can sit in the pocket better than any QB in America. The narrative is that Deshaun Watson is a pass-first dual-threat QB, the most dangerous type.

  • Herbstreit says Oklahoma defense will challenge that system, Galloway says the defensive line better stay in their lanes.

  • Back to Clemson, where we interview...Deshaun Watson..."every game is a new challenge..we're gonna get everyone's best shot."

Jeff climaxes just as Finebaum starts talking about the "Saban vs Mich St" narrative, and the Clemson-Oklahoma rematch, then Alabama-Oklahoma final...suddenly, Kanell blows his load all over Paul as he talks about how lucky Alabama was to get Mich St first..Finebaum opens his mouth and catches some of the shoot in his mouth, and says "This is the first time Danny and I are in agreement all season." The ESPN circle jerk is complete.

Finally, Dantonio:

  • He has the face of a good coach. I don't know what that means, but it's true. Like a thinner Bill Belichick.

  • Regarding Alabama: "I've just got bits and pieces of their games, because they're usually playing the same time as MSU, etc...they're gonna be [insert everything Nick Saban says about his opponents]...then gives nod to B1G by talking about how many members there are now.

Chris Fowler comes on:

  • Says Oklahoma was thrilled at the Committee "snub," that is, dropping them to 4th for not playing...

  • Says Michigan State is the only team who hasn't hit top gear yet, hasn't really played to full potential. This is certainly worrying to me.

  • Rece asks if Chris picks eye test over resume, Chris says it's hard...there's eye tests at certain times in the game, but then there are the numbers

  • Fowler says Henry, Watson, and Mayfield are the Heisman contenders, no disrespect to Christian McCaffery

Bob Stoops on the phone:

  • Oh man, Rece brought up last year's bowl game. Stoops says "uh" 76 times in his next 94 words.

  • What changed after the Texas game? This is the best practice team he's had in 17 years, and they responded well after Texas. The whole team got better.

  • Baker Mayfield (from now on BM) has an infectious personality, and he can run and throw. Some footage shows him doing Manziel-ish things.

  • Rece compared Oklahoma to Ohio State, the #4 seed last year with something to prove. Stoops said he's just gonna practice for Clemson.

Back in the studio:

  • Graphic of Oklahoma revenge games, Oklahoma won their last five. Pollack says that means nothing b/c Clemson is equally motivated to win a national championship.

  • Herbstreit says some teams are more upset than the other team is motivated. He says Oklahoma has that advantage, so Clemson will have to match the intensity that Oklahoma will bring.

  • Galloway says that Oklahoma is the most complete team b/c they have Perine and Mayfield. Bama only has Henry. I don't agree, Coker is a beast-on-call. He's not as "good" as Mayfield right now, but remember that they said the same thing when comparing him to Greyson Lambert. Let's play the game and see for ourselves.
